items: Computational thinking is mainly used for: (a) Playing computer games (b) Solving problems in a logical way (c) Writing essays (d) Drawing pictures
The first step in problem solving is: (a) Writing code (b) Evaluating the solution (c) Identifying the problem (d) Breaking the problem
Breaking a large problem into smaller parts is called: (a) Abstraction (b) Decomposition (c) Evaluation (d) Automation
A step-by-step solution to a problem is known as an: (a) Program (b) Flowchart (c) Algorithm (d) Function
The logic that uses only true or false values is: (a) Predicate logic (b) Fuzzy logic (c) Propositional logic (d) Natural logic
A compound proposition is: (a) (P) (b) (Q) (c) (P∧Q) (d) True
The purpose of a truth table is to: (a) Write programs (b) Store data (c) Evaluate logical expressions (d) Design algorithms
A proposition that is true for at least one case is called: (a) Unsatisfiable (b) Invalid (c) Satisfiable (d) Equivalent
The symbol for the universal quantifier is: (a) ∃ (b) ⟶ (c) ∧ (d) ∀
Predicate logic is mainly used to: (a) Draw diagrams (b) Represent relationships using variables (c) Store numbers (d) Design networks
